text:
The Bruins have lost three straight, outscored 14-4, and the uncomfortable part for anyone panicking is that they played well enough to win more of them. They got 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that stretch. Bad bounces, not a collapse.

The season as a whole runs the other way. Boston is 13-7-1 with 27 points, but our expected points say about 23.5, and the gap comes almost entirely from goaltending: they've allowed nearly 10 fewer goals than the chances against them suggest. Overall the Bruins are a 51% expected-goals team, a bit better at five on five (53%). The engine is the Hampus Lindholm and Charlie McAvoy pair, who own 65% of the expected goals together in 224 minutes, which is the best number on this roster.

The off-ice noise is about Pavel Zacha, with Daily Faceoff asking what the Bruins should do with him and others writing about moving him. James Hagens, the rookie whose line with Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt was outscoring opponents 8-3, is out for what Marco Sturm called a few weeks. Marco Sturm shuffled the forwards again Tuesday against the Kings, per Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub. Our numbers give them 73% playoff odds, but the save percentage they've lived on is the thing to watch.
